alex: Heads-up — ran a quick perf sweep on host-side path for tiny requests (<64 tokens). Seeing ~2.1–2.8ms added on our ingress before it hits the runtime. Notably the tokenizer+parse step is the big chunk.
maria: ugh that explains some tail latency I saw in the dashboards. can you paste the profile?
alex: pasted below, filtered to host process only. main hotspots: tokenize_file (0.9ms), parse_http_frames (0.6ms), grpc_writev_coalesce (0.4ms), header_normalize (0.2ms)
```
# host_profile (p50)
0.90ms tokenize_file
0.60ms parse_http_frames
0.40ms grpc_writev_coalesce
0.20ms header_normalize
0.10ms kv_prefetch_miss
```
devops-bot: deploy/ingress-slim-rc -> started (canary on three hosts) :rocket:
raj: tokenize_file looks heavier than expected — are we doing full unicode normalization per request? any chance to memoize on session id?
alex: we are normalizing + NFKC. For short requests the normalize cost dominates. I tried a quick patch to skip NFKC when request chars < 128 and it shaved ~0.6ms. but need to validate correctness for some CJK customers.
jonah: we also saw extra allocs from the HTTP parser when payload fits in single frame. maybe we can fast-path single-frame JSON without the full state machine.

sam: quick A/B I ran on canary:
- baseline p50 host overhead: 2.3ms p95: 4.8ms
- skip-nfkc p50: 1.7ms p95: 3.9ms
- single-frame-fastpath p50: 1.6ms p95: 3.6ms
maria: nice. Did the skip-nfkc change any model quality tests or tokenization diffs?
alex: ran token-diff on our small prompt suite: 0.03% diffs (mostly in emojis + fullwidth chars). flagged for privacy-sensitive customers only.

raj: another angle — KV cache prefetch miss at 0.1ms in profile but could be amortized by batching prefetches per connection. batching heuristics could pull in top-N cache keys for recently used model and prompt hash.
jonah: agree. also kernel selection: for short sequences we keep a generic kernel which actually has extra setup cost. switching to a short-seq specialized kernel saved ~0.5ms in a microbench. need to evaluate memory/quant tradeoffs.

sam: action items I have:
1) alex to open PR with skip-nfkc + unit tests for edge unicode cases (WIP).
2) jonah to prototype single-frame JSON fastpath in parser.
3) raj to draft KV prefetch batching proposal (2 options: connection-based vs global LRU coalescer).
4) maria to run regression eval on canary traffic for 24h.

alex: will attach PR link once ready. early numbers look promising but we should be careful about correctness for enterprise customers. tagging @security for review on normalization behavior.
maria: thanks — if canary is green after 24h, let's roll to 20% and monitor token-level diffs + p99.

devops-bot: canary -> success (24h) :white_check_mark: hosts: 3 -> metrics: host_overhead.p50 -18% host_overhead.p95 -15%

raj: quick note — if we combine skip-nfkc + short-seq kernel + single-frame fastpath, theoretical p50 host overhead could drop below 1ms for small requests. that would be huge for bursty workloads.

sam: agreed. sounds like a solid plan. I'll consolidate the proposals into a single RFC draft and post here tomorrow. :+1:
